root_cause.text: The GRO completion path in net/core/gro.c incorrectly assumed skb->encapsulation was always clear for RX packets, causing udp4_gro_complete() to use the inner rather than outer network offset when computing the outer UDP pseudo-checksum for encapsulated packets.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states “The udp GRO complete stage assumes that all the packets inserted the RX have the `encapsulation` flag zeroed. Such assumption is not true,” and explains this makes “udp4_gro_complete() use[] the wrong network offset (inner instead of outer)”; the patch fixes it by explicitly clearing the flag in gro_complete() with `skb->encapsulation = 0;`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clear the skb encapsulation flag in gro_complete() so GRO correctly completes packets that NICs deliver as encapsulated.
intent_record.what: A two-line change was added in gro_complete() before rcu_read_lock(): a comment stating that NICs can feed encapsulated packets into GRO, and an assignment setting skb->encapsulation = 0.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this clears the encapsulation flag on the skb before GRO completion handlers run, preventing the packet from continuing to be treated as encapsulated during completion processing and allowing GRO to handle NIC-delivered encapsulated packets correctly.

grouping_result.intent: Clear the skb encapsulation flag in gro_complete() so GRO correctly completes packets that NICs deliver as encapsulated.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by clearing skb->encapsulation in gro_complete(), preventing GRO completion from treating RX packets as encapsulated and thus avoiding use of the inner instead of outer network offset in UDP GRO checksum completion.
